greektrees.book.basics.text: Every tree grows from its own sapling and is built from vanilla blocks; no two grow alike. Saplings can be potted and composted. A tree only grows where all of its wood fits.
greektrees.book.plant.default: Plant on dirt or grass. Grows with light or bone meal.
greektrees.book.cypress.name: Cypress
greektrees.book.cypress.about: Tall, narrow column, 21–23 high. Acacia wood, azalea leaves.
greektrees.book.cypress.lore: Named after Kyparissos, whom Apollo turned into the tree of mourning.
greektrees.book.olive.name: Olive Tree
greektrees.book.olive.about: Short forked trunk with roots, crowns at different heights, 8–12 high. Oak wood, azalea leaves.
greektrees.book.olive.fruit: Olives under the leaves. 2 hunger; eating one leaves a pit.
greektrees.book.fig.name: Fig Tree
greektrees.book.fig.about: Low and wide, several stems, 7 high. Acacia wood, azalea leaves.
greektrees.book.fig.lore: Figs fed the first athletes of Olympia.
greektrees.book.strawberry_tree.name: Strawberry Tree
greektrees.book.strawberry_tree.about: Thin orange-red stems, open dark crown, 10–11 high. Stripped acacia wood, mangrove leaves.
greektrees.book.strawberry_tree.lore: Its berries take a year to ripen, so flowers and fruit hang side by side.
greektrees.book.strawberry_tree.fruit: Arbutus berries under the leaves. 3 hunger.
greektrees.book.date_palm.name: Cretan Date Palm
greektrees.book.date_palm.about: One to three slim, leaning trunks, 15–18 high. Jungle wood, jungle leaves.
greektrees.book.date_palm.lore: The Cretan date palm, named after Theophrastus, grows wild on the beach of Vai.
greektrees.book.date_palm.plant: On dirt, grass or sand. Four in a square grow a large palm.
greektrees.book.date_palm.fruit: Dates on the trunk, right under the crown. 3 hunger.
greektrees.book.mulberry.name: Mulberry Tree
greektrees.book.mulberry.about: Short thick trunk under a dense round dome, 10–11 high. Acacia wood, jungle leaves.
greektrees.book.mulberry.lore: Once white, the berries turned dark with the blood of Pyramus.
greektrees.book.mulberry.fruit: Black, white or red mulberries, one kind per tree. 2 hunger.
greektrees.book.weeping_willow.name: Weeping Willow
greektrees.book.weeping_willow.about: Softly bent trunk, a curtain of leaf strands with room inside, 11–21 high. Acacia wood, mangrove leaves, vines.
greektrees.book.weeping_willow.lore: Orpheus carried a willow branch into the underworld.
greektrees.book.weeping_willow.plant: Plant on dirt or grass. Grows with light or bone meal. Four in a square grow a big willow.
greektrees.book.aries_oak.name: Aries Oak
greektrees.book.aries_oak.about: A giant, 53–60 high and as wide, with hollow crowns to build in. Its leaves never decay.
greektrees.book.aries_oak.lore: Like the oak of Dodona, in whose leaves Zeus was heard.
greektrees.book.aries_oak.plant: Only grows from 16 saplings in a 4×4 square. Fewer never grow and take no bone meal.
greektrees.book.large_date_palm.name: Large Date Palm
greektrees.book.large_date_palm.about: Two to five tall trunks slanting apart, 19–27 high.
greektrees.book.large_weeping_willow.abo: A 2×2 trunk and more strands along the rim, 15–25 high.
greektrees.book.fruit.text: Fruit ripens in three stages, like cocoa; bone meal helps. Right click ripe fruit: 2–3 fruit, the twig stays and starts over. Breaking unripe fruit gives one. Plant fruit on a leaf block to hang a new twig; dates go on the side of jungle wood. Breaking a tree's leaves sometimes drops fruit.
greektrees.book.pits.text: Eating an olive leaves a pit. Throw it like a snowball, by hand or from a dispenser: 1.5 hearts. Two pits on top of each other make a sharpened pit: 3.5 hearts. Both break on impact.
